The Crop Analytics Orchestra

Source: vignettes/crop_analytics_orchestra.Rmd
crop_analytics_orchestra.Rmd
library(cropOrchestra)

Why

I have R installed, a nitrogen-rate decision to make, and a colleague’s word that an “orchestra” of packages can carry it from raw paddock data to a defensible number; there are fifteen of them, several are not on CRAN, and before I trust any of it I want to know what is actually here, what each piece is for, and whether I can check that for myself rather than take it on faith. What is cropOrchestra, and how do I find out what I have? This is the question an agronomist, analyst or breeder asks the first time somebody hands them the Crop Analytics Orchestra rather than a single package: not “how does the mathematics work” but “what is actually here, and can I trust the list”. cropOrchestra answers it directly. It is not itself an analytical package – it ships no models – it is the front door: a roster, a version checker, an installer, and a gate runner over the released members. The other packages in the orchestra take a grain-production question – which nitrogen rate, which variety, when to test, when to harvest – from raw data to a recorded decision, and refuse rather than guess where the evidence does not support one; every hand-off between them is a typed manifest, every abstention is a typed refusal rather than a silent NA, and every external fact a package relies on carries provenance back to its source. When the whole chain was run end to end on a synthetic barley belt (Study A0), it returned a headline number that beat a naive baseline by a wide margin; this vignette does not rerun that chain, so the number itself, and the sentence that says it is not recomputed here, are held for Limits. What this vignette does show, on this machine, right now, is what cropOrchestra itself can check without running a single crop model: which packages are on the release roster, which of them are actually installed, and whether the two agree.

What

cao_roster() returns the fifteen-member release roster frozen on 2026-09-02: nine core members that every study routes through, and six supporting members that particular studies need, each row carrying its tier, its necessity-register role, the max578 repository it publishes through, and whether that repository is public yet. A member earns its row by answering four questions in the release’s necessity register: which crop question needs it, what the nearest tool outside the orchestra is, why that outside tool does not suffice – one of four admissible reasons: a missing capability, a contract the pipeline requires that the outside tool cannot emit, an independent-oracle grounding it does not carry, or a translation layer that does not exist outside – and where it was load-bearing in a study, an arbitration, or a fleet gate. The method statement behind every member is the same three-step discipline: the orchestra picks the best available method, old or new, its own or external, adopts or adapts it behind the typed-manifest contract, and translates it into a grower- or breeder-facing decision. A member that only adapts an external tool – wrapping it behind the contract rather than adding new mathematics – is justified by the contract alone, and the register says so plainly rather than overstating its novelty.

cao_versions() joins that fixed roster with what this R session can actually load: an installed_version column read through requireNamespace() rather than a hard library() call, so a member whose repository is still private is reported as not installed rather than raising an error, plus a match column recording whether the installed version equals the frozen one.

cao_status() turns that join into a report: every member classified as installed and matching, installed but drifted, or missing, and for every missing member, a stated reason – its repository is not yet public, or it is public but not yet mirrored on max578.r-universe.dev.

cao_install() installs a tier ("core", "supporting", "all") or an explicit set of package names, one member at a time, from the max578 r-universe mirror and CRAN, so one member’s still-private repository never stops the rest from installing; dry_run = TRUE resolves and returns the plan without installing anything, which is what the next section runs.

cao_check() goes one step further than a status report: pointed at a local ORCHESTRA leader workspace, it runs the fleet’s own gate scripts – the cross-member refusal contract and the manifest conformance suite – and reports pass or fail for each; without a workspace, it falls back to cao_status() plus a load check of every member that is installed.

Do

The roster, as frozen 

roster <- cao_roster()
nrow(roster)
#> [1] 15
attr(roster, "freeze_date")
#> [1] "2026-09-02"
The frozen roster (15 members, freeze 2026-09-02).
Member Tier Role

PESTO core simulator inversion + ensemble UQ

apsimR core the mechanism member

cdzoo supporting the causal-discovery harness

What is actually installed on this machine

cao_status() prints its own report, so the table below is read straight from the console, not retyped.

status <- cao_status()
#> Crop Analytics Orchestra -- status at freeze 2026-09-02 
#>   0 matching, 15 drifted, 0 missing (of 15 members)
#> 
#>   [I] flexyBayes           frozen 0.10.0     installed 0.18.1     (core) 
#>   [I] PESTO                frozen 0.10.1     installed 0.11.1.9000 (core) 
#>   [I] kernR                frozen 0.8.2      installed 0.10.0.9000 (core) 
#>   [I] apsimR               frozen 0.3.0      installed 0.3.2.9000 (core) 
#>   [I] quorum               frozen 0.1.0      installed 0.1.0.9000 (core) 
#>   [I] terroir              frozen 0.2.0      installed 0.4.0.9000 (core) 
#>   [I] masque               frozen 0.11.0     installed 0.15.0     (core) 
#>   [I] decideR              frozen 0.1.0      installed 0.3.1.9000 (core) 
#>   [I] grainPlan            frozen 0.1.1      installed 0.2.1.9000 (core) 
#>   [I] gpfield              frozen 0.3.0      installed 0.4.1.9000 (supporting) 
#>   [I] kalmix               frozen 0.5.0      installed 0.6.0.9000 (supporting) 
#>   [I] koine                frozen 0.3.0      installed 0.3.1.9000 (supporting) 
#>   [I] proxymix             frozen 0.15.2     installed 0.17.0     (supporting) 
#>   [I] optimix              frozen 0.1.0      installed 0.2.0.9000 (supporting) 
#>   [I] cdzoo                frozen 0.2.0      installed 0.2.0.9000 (supporting)
plot_df <- status$versions
plot_df$member <- factor(plot_df$member, levels = rev(plot_df$member))
plot_df$tier_label <- ifelse(
  plot_df$tier == "core",
  paste0("core (", sum(plot_df$tier == "core"), ")"),
  paste0("supporting (", sum(plot_df$tier == "supporting"), ")")
)
plot_df$status_label <- gsub("_", " ", plot_df$status, fixed = TRUE)
ggplot2::ggplot(
  plot_df, ggplot2::aes(x = 1L, y = member, fill = status_label)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile(width = 0.9, height = 0.85, colour = "white") +
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    ggplot2::aes(label = paste0(
      version, " / ",
      ifelse(is.na(installed_version), "-", installed_version)
    )),
    colour = "white", size = 3
  ) +
  ggplot2::facet_grid(tier_label ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
    name = "status",
    values = c(
      "installed matching" = "#0072B2",
      "installed drifted" = "#D55E00",
      "missing" = "#999999"
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    title = "Roster status at the 2026-09-02 freeze, this machine"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    strip.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 0)
  )

Every roster member at the 2026-09-02 freeze, grouped by tier and coloured by whether the version installed on this machine matches the frozen release, has drifted ahead of it, or is not installed here; the label in each cell reads frozen version / installed version.

Planning an install without touching anything 

plan <- cao_install(members = "core", dry_run = TRUE)
The resolved install plan for the core tier (9 members); dry run, nothing installed.

# Installs whatever in the plan above is not already present. Skipped here
# because rendering this vignette must never modify the R library it runs
# in; run this line yourself against your own library to install the core
# tier for real.
cao_install(members = "core")

Checking the fleet’s own gates 

check_fallback <- cao_check()
check_fallback$n_loadable
#> [1] 15
check_fallback$n_load_failed
#> [1] 0
# Needs a local ORCHESTRA leader workspace (not shipped with this package)
# whose integration/ directory holds the fleet's gate scripts. Skipped here
# because the path below is specific to the machine this vignette was
# written on, not portable to a reader's own layout.
cao_check(workspace = "/path/to/ORCHESTRA_dev")

Read

Of the 15 roster members, 9 are core and 6 are supporting; 8 of the 15 (53 per cent, roughly half) are on a private repository at the freeze date, and cao_status() says so plainly, member by member, rather than presenting a partial install as if the roster installs in full today.

On the machine this vignette was rendered on, 0 members match their frozen version exactly and 0 are missing. 15 members have drifted ahead of its frozen version rather than behind it: flexyBayes (frozen 0.10.0, installed 0.18.1), PESTO (frozen 0.10.1, installed 0.11.1.9000), kernR (frozen 0.8.2, installed 0.10.0.9000), apsimR (frozen 0.3.0, installed 0.3.2.9000), quorum (frozen 0.1.0, installed 0.1.0.9000), terroir (frozen 0.2.0, installed 0.4.0.9000), masque (frozen 0.11.0, installed 0.15.0), decideR (frozen 0.1.0, installed 0.3.1.9000), grainPlan (frozen 0.1.1, installed 0.2.1.9000), gpfield (frozen 0.3.0, installed 0.4.1.9000), kalmix (frozen 0.5.0, installed 0.6.0.9000), koine (frozen 0.3.0, installed 0.3.1.9000), proxymix (frozen 0.15.2, installed 0.17.0), optimix (frozen 0.1.0, installed 0.2.0.9000), cdzoo (frozen 0.2.0, installed 0.2.0.9000).

Of the 15 installed members here, 15 load cleanly through requireNamespace() and 0 do not. The figure shows the same three-way split by tier: a reader can see at a glance whether drift, where it exists, clusters in the core tier every study routes through or in the supporting tier particular studies need, which the roster table above does not show without reading all 15 rows.

Limits

This vignette shows what cropOrchestra itself can determine without touching a crop model: a roster, a version comparison, and a load check. It does not run apsimR, does not fit anything through kernR or flexyBayes, and does not price a decision through decideR – it cannot speak to whether any member’s science is correct, only to whether the member is present and at the frozen version. The install call above is a dry run for the same reason cao_check(workspace = ...) above is not evaluated: rendering this vignette must never modify the R library it runs in, and the workspace path is specific to the machine it was written on rather than portable to a reader’s own layout; a reader who wants either result runs the commands shown, verbatim, against their own library and their own copy of the ORCHESTRA leader workspace.

The headline claim behind the necessity register – that when the roster’s core chain (apsimR + quorum + PESTO as the mechanism lens, kernR as the field-agreement lens, decideR as the decision lens, optimix as the site-value lens, and grainPlan as the grower-facing translation) was run end to end on a synthetic barley belt, the orchestra’s cascade lost 2,960 AUD per hectare against the planted truth over 198 decision cells, against 5,818 AUD per hectare for a naive mechanism-only arm – 49 per cent less loss, reproducing on a re-seeded belt – is not recomputed in this vignette; it is cited to Study A0’s own ledger (studies/A0/REPORT.md and SUMMARY.md in the ORCHESTRA leader workspace) and should be read there, not trusted from this paragraph alone. It is a controlled recovery exercise on a synthetic belt, not a real one: the shape of the result has real-data cover – the belt’s nitrogen-response slopes partially bracket a real barley multi-environment trial – but the magnitudes do not, and they should never be quoted as a field result. cao_status() and cao_check() exist precisely so a claim like this one is always read alongside what is actually installed and actually gated on the machine making the claim, not asserted from memory.

Everything numeric in Read above describes one machine at one moment: a different library, a package upgraded after this vignette was rendered, or the roster’s next freeze would all change the counts without changing anything this vignette asserts about how to find them out.

What to read next

A quorum of lenses on Study A0 (in quorum) resolves the same 200 recorded decision cells the headline number above comes from, lens by lens, and is the closest a reader can get to the cascade’s mechanics without rerunning the study. From an inference result to a grain plan (in grainPlan) picks up exactly where this front door leaves off, turning a manifest-typed inference result into a grower-facing plan. Getting started with decideR introduces the decision lens the headline cascade above relies on.

Reproduce

This vignette draws no random numbers and calls no external service: every table and figure is a deterministic function of the roster shipped inside this package and of what is installed in the R library it is rendered against, which is why the counts above are read live rather than typed by hand.
